author: TEDx Talks
description:
In 2008, Tonantzin Carmona's family lost their home — one foreclosure notice among millions. She took two lessons from that wreckage: a financial system can collapse on people who had no hand in building it, and when it does, the people who did build it rarely pay. She's hearing the same warning signals now, in crypto.

Her argument isn't that crypto is a bad bet. It's that you're already exposed whether or not you ever touch it. Pension funds and 401(k)s, your energy bill, scams clustered in working-class neighborhoods — the risk has quietly crossed from Wall Street to Main Street. And the newest weak link, stablecoins, ties this volatile market back to ordinary banks and Treasury bonds, so the next panic might not spread one foreclosure at a time. It could spread at the speed of code.

Underneath the finance is a harder question about who gets to write the rules. With crypto money now bankrolling a huge share of our politics and regulators loosening the guardrails, Carmona asks whet
title: How cryptocurrency creates risks for everyone | Tonantzin Carmona | TEDxMidAtlantic

What happens when one online mistake follows someone for the rest of their life? In this talk, Emma Dutta argues for the Right to Be Forgotten, a legal idea that allows people to request the removal of outdated, irrelevant, or harmful personal data. Through examples of digital permanence, online misinformation, and reputation damage, she explains why privacy laws such as the GDPR matter in giving people the chance to grow beyond their past.

This talk invites us to rethink one of the most misunderstood transitions in a woman's life. AIが急速に進化する今、私たちは人間らしさの根本である「生きがい」を失う危機に瀕しているのでしょうか？
脳科学者の茂木健一郎氏が、外部評価のみで学習するAIと、日常の「小さな喜び」を原動力とする人間の決定的な違いを紐解きます。他人の評価に依存しない自分だけの喜びこそが、人間の創造性と幸福の真の源泉であると解説。AIと調和し、より豊かで楽観的な未来を築くための鍵となる「生きがい」の力に迫る必見のトークです。


As artificial intelligence grows exponentially, are we at risk of losing the very essence of what makes us human?
In this insightful talk, neuroscientist Ken Mogi explores the critical crossroads of our future with AI. While artificial intelligence relies entirely on external scores to learn, humans thrive on "Ikigai"—finding deep, intrinsic joy in everyday moments.  Mogi reveals how our private, unrewarded joys are the true source of human creativity. Discover why embracing your own "Ikigai" is the key to ensuring a harmonious and optimistic future alongside AI. 脳科学者、作家、キャスター。屋久島おおぞら高校校長。東京大学大学院特任教授及び客員教授。「クオリア」を中心とする脳科学、認知科学、及び、人工知能と人間の脳の関係の研究に取り組む。2005年、『脳と仮想』（新潮社）で第4回小林秀雄賞。2009年、『今、ここからすべての場所へ』（筑摩書房）で第12回桑原武夫学芸賞。

This lecture is based on previously published research and articles that analyze the phenomenon of games not only from the perspective of entertainment, but also through the lens of media ecology. The “invisible revolution” in my topic refers to game design that incorporates sustainability principles in a fluid way, without feeling like a theoretical lesson.

In the environmental and economic context, *Dave the Diver* functions as a virtual laboratory. The player must fish in order to sustain a restaurant, but if marine resources are depleted in a predatory way, the game imposes consequences. It teaches the concept of responsible consumption and production, aligned with SDGs 12 and 14.

In the social context, *Pokémon GO* changed urban dynamics by encouraging health and well-being, aligned with SDG 3, while also re-signifying parks and neighborhoods around the world and promoting real human interactions through a digital interface.

author: TEDx Talks
description:
This lecture proposes an in-depth analysis of how Artificial Intelligence is redefining human and professional relationships. The focus is on the conflict of adaptation that both connects and distances Boomers, with their vast accumulated experience, and Generation X, which seeks the practical usefulness of these tools.

We move through Millennials, or Generation Y, who occupy the role of a bridge between the analog and the digital, until we reach Generation Z and Generation Alpha, who already breathe the algorithm natively.

At the heart of the discussion is a warning about the outsourcing of critical thinking. Without a conscious generational exchange, we risk entering an empty cycle in which AI produces content for AI itself to consume, leaving human beings as extras in their own intellect.
 Luis é Coordenador na UniFECAF, Gestor Educacional e Engenheiro de Software com mestrado em Ciências da Computação. Com uma trajetória focada na interseção entre ensino e tecnologia ele também
title: The Prompt War: How Each Generation Survives in AI | Luis Pires | TEDxFECAP

This lecture starts from that case to discuss why algorithmic accountability in Brazil is still an empty promise, and why change needs to begin in the classrooms where technology is taught.

As a technology professor, I realized that we teach how algorithms work, but we do not teach whom they are meant to serve.

title: Who Is Accountable for the Algorithm? | Francisco Escobar | TEDxFECAP

author: TEDx Talks
description:
We are constantly encouraged to persist, not to give up, and to maintain discipline as the main path to success. However, little is said about the risk of consistently moving in the wrong direction. In an increasingly dynamic and uncertain world, the ability to adjust course becomes just as important as discipline itself.

This lecture is relevant because it proposes a shift in mindset: moving away from the logic of repetition and toward the logic of strategic reflection. More than doing more, it is necessary to better understand where one is heading.

By presenting a clear and applicable method, the idea helps individuals develop greater awareness of their decisions, avoid unproductive cycles, and build paths that are more aligned with their goals. In a context where time, energy, and focus are scarce resources, learning how to recalibrate the path may be the true difference between effort and evolution.
 Antonio Emanuel Andrade e Silva é Major da Polícia Militar do Estado de São Pau
title: Discipline Is Not Enough: Adjusting the Course of Your Life. | Emanuel Andrade e Silva | TEDxFECAP

author: TEDx Talks
description:
The battle for attention has always existed, but it has never taken place on such an intense scale as it does today. While brands once competed for space in newspapers, radio, or television, today they compete for precious seconds inside devices we carry with us all the time.

Faced with thousands of daily stimuli, a fundamental question emerges: how can we distinguish what truly matters? This lecture seeks to discuss not only how brands and platforms capture our attention, but especially how individuals can develop a more conscious relationship with information consumption, recovering autonomy in an environment designed to constantly compete for their focus.
 Sócio-fundador e Diretor de Mídia da CreativosBR, agência responsável por contas como QuintoAndar, Hospital Albert Einstein, GrandVision e Placar. Publicitário, mestre em Administração pela FECAP e especialista em mídia e estratégia, construiu sua carreira em algumas das principais agências do país, atendendo marcas como Bradesc

description:
Bioinformatics connects biology, technology, data analysis, and physiology, showing how different fields can work together to understand the functioning of the human body. We live in an era in which biological data is growing at an exponential rate, and bioinformatics is the key to transforming this information into useful knowledge for healthcare.

It allows physiological processes to be interpreted with greater precision, contributing to more effective diagnoses and treatments. It also plays a fundamental role in public health, helping to monitor diseases, predict outbreaks, and guide prevention policies.

Atualmente cursa Ciência de Dados pela Universidade Federal do Mato Grosso do Sul, ampliando sua atuação na intersecção entre educação, ciência e tecnologia.
